title: Past continuous vs past simple
goal: Contar incidentes e historias: qué estaba pasando cuando ocurrió algo.

vocabulary.example: The server crashed while I was deploying.
The app crashed during the demo.
Suddenly, the connection dropped.
We wrote a report about the incident.
I noticed the error in the logs.

exercises.prompt: I ___ the database when the power went out.
exercises.explanation: Pasado continuo (was/were + -ing) = acción larga en progreso. Pasado simple = acción corta que la interrumpe: 'I was updating... when the power went out'.

exercises.prompt: They ___ testing the app when we called. (to be, pasado)
exercises.explanation: Pasado de 'to be': 'was' con I / he / she / it y 'were' con you / we / they → 'they were testing'.

exercises.prompt: ___ I was presenting, my internet connection dropped.
exercises.explanation: 'While' + oración (sujeto + verbo). 'During' + sustantivo: 'during the presentation'. Error típico: 'during I was presenting'.

exercises.prompt: Estaba revisando los logs cuando noté el error.
answers: I was checking the logs when I noticed the error
I was reviewing the logs when I noticed the error
I was looking at the logs when I noticed the error
exercises.explanation: 'Estaba revisando' = 'was checking' (en progreso); 'noté' = 'noticed' (acción puntual). Ambos sujetos se repiten en inglés: 'I was..., when I noticed'.

exercises.passage: Incident summary: On Tuesday at 10:15, while the team was running a database migration, the payment service stopped responding. Ana noticed the alerts and paused the migration. The service recovered at 10:40. Root cause: the migration was locking a table that the payment service needed.
exercises.prompt: ¿Qué estaba haciendo el equipo cuando falló el servicio?
options: Ejecutando una migración de base de datos
exercises.explanation: 'While the team was running a database migration' = mientras el equipo estaba ejecutando una migración. El pasado continuo describe la acción de fondo.

exercises.passage: Incident summary: On Tuesday at 10:15, while the team was running a database migration, the payment service stopped responding. Ana noticed the alerts and paused the migration. The service recovered at 10:40. Root cause: the migration was locking a table that the payment service needed.
exercises.prompt: ¿Cuál fue la causa raíz (root cause)?
options: La migración bloqueaba una tabla que necesitaba el servicio de pagos
El servicio de pagos tenía un bug
exercises.explanation: 'The migration was locking a table that the payment service needed'. 'Root cause' es un término clave en reportes de incidentes (post-mortems).

title: Gerunds vs infinitives
goal: Saber qué forma va después de verbos como enjoy, want, avoid o decide.

vocabulary.example: I enjoy solving problems.
Avoid sending emails late at night.
We decided to use React.
I'm used to working with US teams.
Have you considered moving abroad?

exercises.prompt: I really enjoy ___ with international teams.
exercises.explanation: Después de enjoy, avoid, finish, consider, mind y suggest va -ing: 'I enjoy working'.

exercises.prompt: We decided ___ the launch until Monday.
exercises.explanation: Después de decide, want, plan, need, hope, agree y offer va 'to' + verbo: 'We decided to postpone'.

exercises.prompt: I'm interested in ___ more about your company. (learn)
exercises.explanation: Después de cualquier preposición (in, about, of, for, at, without) el verbo va en -ing: 'interested in learning', 'good at solving'.

exercises.prompt: I'm used to ___ early because of the time difference.
exercises.explanation: 'Be used to' = estar acostumbrado a, y aquí 'to' es preposición → -ing: 'I'm used to waking up early'. No confundir con 'used to + verbo' (solía).

exercises.prompt: Evita enviar correos largos.
exercises.explanation: 'Avoid' + -ing: 'Avoid sending'. Y el adjetivo va antes del sustantivo: 'long emails'.

exercises.prompt: "I stopped to check my email" significa...
options: Me detuve (paré lo que hacía) para revisar mi correo
exercises.explanation: 'Stop + to' = parar PARA hacer algo. 'Stop + -ing' = dejar de hacer algo: 'I stopped checking my email' = dejé de revisarlo.

title: The passive voice
goal: Describir procesos y resultados cuando importa la acción más que quién la hizo.

vocabulary.example: The budget was approved yesterday.
Version 2.0 will be released in May.
The data is stored in the cloud.
The requirements were changed.
The ticket was assigned to me.

exercises.prompt: All user data ___ in encrypted form.
exercises.explanation: Voz pasiva = to be + participio. En presente: 'is stored' (se almacena). Se usa mucho en documentación técnica.

exercises.prompt: The ticket ___ assigned to me yesterday. (to be, pasado)
exercises.explanation: Pasiva en pasado: was / were + participio. 'The ticket was assigned to me' (me asignaron el ticket).

exercises.prompt: El presupuesto fue aprobado ayer.
exercises.explanation: 'Fue aprobado' = 'was approved'. Estructura: sujeto + was/were + participio.

exercises.prompt: The new version ___ next month.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva en futuro: will be + participio. La versión no se lanza a sí misma, alguien la lanza → 'will be released'.

exercises.prompt: ¿Cómo se dice 'Se habla inglés en todas las reuniones'?
options: It speaks English in all meetings.
English is spoken in all meetings.
Is spoken English in all meetings.
exercises.explanation: El 'se' impersonal del español suele traducirse con voz pasiva: 'English is spoken...'. 'It speaks' significaría que 'algo' habla.
Pasiva en presente perfecto: have / has + been + participio. 'The requirements have been changed' (han cambiado los requisitos).

title: Relative clauses & reported speech
title_es: Oraciones de relativo y estilo indirecto
goal: Dar más detalle con who / which / that y contar lo que otra persona dijo.

vocabulary.example: She's the engineer who built the API.
The tool, which is free, works well.
He mentioned that the deadline changed.
She told me she was busy.
Can you explain how it works?

exercises.prompt: We need someone ___ has experience with AWS.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' para personas, 'which' para cosas, 'that' para ambas (en oraciones sin comas). 'What' NO es pronombre relativo: 'someone what...' es un error típico.

exercises.prompt: This is the library ___ we use for testing.
exercises.explanation: Para cosas: 'that' o 'which'. En este tipo de frase también se puede omitir: 'This is the library we use for testing'.

exercises.prompt: She ___ me that the client was happy.
exercises.explanation: 'Tell' necesita a la persona: 'told ME'. 'Say' no: 'she said (that)...'. Incorrecto: 'she said me'.

exercises.prompt: Direct: "I am busy." → Reported: He said he ___ busy. (to be)
exercises.explanation: En estilo indirecto el verbo suele 'retroceder' un tiempo: am / is → was, will → would, can → could.

exercises.prompt: Direct: "We will send the files tomorrow." → They said they ___ the files the next day.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' pasa a 'would' en estilo indirecto. También cambian las referencias de tiempo: tomorrow → the next day.

exercises.prompt: Ella es la ingeniera que construyó la API.
answers: She is the engineer who built the API
She's the engineer who built the API
She is the engineer that built the API
She's the engineer that built the API
exercises.explanation: Para personas: 'who' (o 'that'). 'Construyó' = 'built' (pasado irregular de 'build').
